claimPolicy.rule: Public capability claims must stay support-graded and evidence-linked. Broad comparative marketing terms are not permitted in authored public surfaces.

languageTiers.description: Behavior is defined over Unicode code points or strings without language-specific claims.
Behavior is demonstrated only on committed fixture slices.
Behavior depends on committed resources with license and provenance metadata.
Behavior or readiness has executed comparator captures with named versions and documented differences.
Behavior is evaluated against a committed or reproducibly fetched corpus slice with declared scope.

axes.label: Task coverage
axes.measurement: Each NLP task has a declared support status and linked evidence.
axes.gate: No task claim may exceed its support status in support-status.v1.json.

axes.label: Language tier
axes.measurement: Each task states the strongest language tier supported by current evidence.
axes.gate: A language tier requires the minimum evidence listed in this scorecard.

axes.label: Comparator evidence
axes.measurement: Comparator captures name tool versions, fixture inputs, outputs, and differences.
axes.gate: Comparator-backed claims require replayable capture artifacts.

axes.label: Corpus evidence
axes.measurement: Corpus-backed claims name corpus provenance, slice policy, and conformance reports.
axes.gate: Corpus-backed claims require persisted corpus slices or reproducible fetch instructions.

axes.label: Conformance
axes.measurement: Machine-readable reports connect claims to checks and evidence.
axes.gate: Implemented task claims require conformance reports.

axes.label: API
axes.measurement: Public APIs are exported from package entrypoints and covered by tests.
axes.gate: Package rows cannot advance without exported runtime and type surfaces.

axes.label: Performance
axes.measurement: Throughput, memory, and scale thresholds are declared before broad operational claims.
axes.gate: Broad corpus or pipeline claims require performance regression thresholds.

axes.label: Release readiness
axes.measurement: Packages pass metadata, build, export, and package-quality checks.
axes.gate: Package adoption claims require release gates to pass.

axes.label: Security
axes.measurement: Dependency and generated-artifact changes are explicit and auditable.
axes.gate: New runtime dependencies require review and lockfile evidence.

axes.label: Reproducibility
axes.measurement: Evidence can be replayed from committed inputs and pinned commands.
axes.gate: Claims require deterministic replay or a documented blocker.

packageRows.nextGate: Keep cross-package protocol, conformance, and resource growth outside textfacts.
Expand graph conventions only through validated fixtures and schemas.
Add resource review and registry workflow before broad resource claims.
Keep rule behavior fixture-scoped until comparator-backed language slices expand.
Define async, streaming, batching, and cache contracts before implementation.
Add retrieval readiness before query, snippet, and relevance behavior.
Add version negotiation only after a public contract exists.
Add diff and report rendering before wider benchmark use.
Add evidence inspection for comparator drift, diffs, and support matrices.

taskRows.nextGate: Expand multilingual fixtures and comparator replay breadth before broader claims.
Validate dependency, relation, entity-linking, and coreference graph examples.
Add public resource review and update policy.
Add a second executed comparator or reduce the stated comparator-backed scope.
Add multilingual negative controls and entity-linking readiness.
Add retrieval readiness with query, snippet, and relevance fixtures.
Broaden invalid fixtures and keep parser behavior separate from format round-trip.
Add broader UD treebank slices, performance thresholds, and JavaScript gap resolution before parser behavior.

releaseGates.description: Package metadata names, exports, files, side effects, and license are explicit.
Package tests exercise runtime guards, schemas, and public examples.
Repository and package schemas validate under the declared drafts.
Package-quality checks run before publication decisions.
Dependency changes and workflow evidence are reviewed before release.

antiMetricPolicy: A numeric score is only an inspection aid. It cannot widen a support claim without linked fixtures, validators, comparator captures, and conformance reports.
